what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/know-who-is-in-this: keep a person's voice or face print only with consent words, name who said each stretch of a transcript, find and name the faces in a picture or video, list the people the prints can name, keep who appeared in a recording as rows linked to the person, and read where someone appeared.

payload.label: Teach listening someone's voice or face
payload.job: Teach this person's computer to recognise someone, by a recording of their voice, a picture of their face, or a voice it already heard while listening, so what they say is named as theirs
payload.description: Runs on the person's computer. Give name, kind (voice or face) and consent (who agreed to be known here, and how: nobody is enrolled without it), and one of: path (a file on the computer), file (a recording or picture in their files), or heard_voice (a voice the computer heard while listening, like voice-2, from the listening that was running at heard_at, the time a turn of that voice was said, else the latest unless session names one); everything that voice already said in that listening is then named as theirs too. me true marks the person themselves, so their words arrive as theirs. A face enrollment keeps their picture. Several samples make it surer: enroll again to add one.

name.description: The person's name, as their words should be named

consent.description: Who agreed to be recognised here, and how, like "Sam said yes in the 3 Oct standup"

path.description: A recording or picture on the computer

file.description: A recording or picture in the person's files, by name or identity

heard_voice.description: A voice heard while listening, like voice-2, as a turn named it (Someone (voice-2))

session.description: The listening session the voice was heard in; the latest when left out

heard_at.description: When a turn of that voice was said (the turn message's time), so the right listening is found

me.description: true when this is the person themselves

payload.label: Enrol someone's voice or face so they can be named
payload.job: Let the person's AI name this person later by their voice or face, after they agreed to be known that way
payload.description: Measures a recording of one person speaking, or a picture or video of one person's face, or takes a voice heard in a listening, and keeps it as that person's print so later recordings and pictures can name them. It refuses before it measures anything unless `consent` says who agreed to be known by their voice or face and how. Enrolling the same name again adds samples and the new consent words to the same print and keeps the earlier ones. The voice-print, face-print and listening-voices record kinds are stays_on_this_device: true: the numbers of a print are kept only on the device they were made on and are never shared, exported, synced or sent to a model off it. The answer says how many samples the person has, never the numbers.

kind.description: Enrol a voice or a face

name.x-free-text-because: The name of the person being enrolled, as they want it said.

consent.description: Who agreed to be known by their voice or face, and how (for example: said yes in the team call on Monday)
consent.x-free-text-because: The words that record who agreed and how; they are kept with the print.

me.description: True when this is the person who owns the records

file.description: A recording of the person speaking, or a picture or video of their face, by identity in your files

heard_voice.description: Instead of a file, for a voice: a label such as voice-3 heard in `listening`

payload.description: Takes a recording and answers each turn with who said it. A supplied transcript is reused; otherwise tools/audio-transcription's existing Whisper engine chooser hears the bounded recording first. Its selected local provider may fetch public model weights; missing engines or models fail rather than inventing words. The person's name is given when one enrolled person is clearly the closest voice; every person it could be when two are too close to tell, so a guess is never made silently; otherwise an unknown voice with a number that stays the same for the whole listening, across every recording of it. Stretches of one voice are judged together, a stretch too short to measure takes its neighbour's voice, and turns of one voice a couple of seconds apart are joined. Thresholds, the wording of the labels and the gap that joins turns are inputs; the starting values are not yet calibrated on the person's own consented clips. The voice-print and listening-voices record kinds are stays_on_this_device: true: only the listening's listening-voices record is kept, with the numbers of the unknown voices heard, on this device. It names no one who has not enrolled.

file.description: The recording (audio or video), by identity in your files

text.x-free-text-because: Words the recording's transcript says, passed through to the turn that holds them.

listening.description: The listening this recording belongs to; unknown voices keep their number across all its recordings

rules.description: Thresholds: person_at_least, sure_by, maybe_at_least, same_unknown_at_least, same_in_piece_at_least, shortest_seconds, new_voice_shortest_seconds

words.description: Wording of the labels: unknown (with {voice}), unsure (with {names}), or

join_within_seconds.description: Turns of one voice this close are joined (default 2)

max_seconds.description: How many seconds of the recording to measure (default 3600)

voice_sessions.description: Voices heard in listenings; filled automatically

payload.label: Find the faces in a picture or video and say who they are
payload.job: Find every face in a picture or video and name the ones that belong to people who agreed to be known
payload.description: Finds the faces in a picture, or in a picture taken from a video every few seconds, and answers each face's place (the second, the box in pixels) and who it is: the person's name when one enrolled face is clearly the closest, every person it could be when two are too close to tell, nobody otherwise. Changes no file. Thresholds are inputs; the starting values are not yet calibrated on the person's own consented pictures. The face-print record kind is stays_on_this_device: true: prints are read here and never leave the device they were made on.

payload.label: Keep who appeared in a recording
payload.job: Work out the rows that link each person whose voice was heard or face seen in a recording to that recording, the seconds and the place, for the person's list of where people appeared
payload.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Takes what tool:who-is-in-this answered (heard) and what tool:find-faces answered (seen) about one recording and answers one row per stretch (rows) for the person's Where people appeared list, for you to keep: who, heard or seen, recording, start and end seconds, the words said, the place it was recorded, and the person's own row when given. A person is named only when the answer named them, and only while their voice-print or face-print is handed in with consent words (consents, read from the prints without their numbers): a person with none refuses the answer. An unsure stretch keeps the people it could be and an unknown voice keeps its number, so enrolling that voice later names what was kept; a face nobody enrolled is not answered. The same answer again is the same row ids; a changed answer answers the rows it replaces as superseded_rows (earlier, the appearance records already kept for this recording, tells which) and deletes none. list is the list definition to make if it is not there yet. No row holds a print's numbers.

listening.description: The listening it belongs to, as given to tool:who-is-in-this

consents.description: The consent words of each print the answer names, read from the prints without their numbers: [{ how: voice or face, person, consent: [words] }]

earlier.description: The appearance records already kept for this recording, [{ id, value }], so rows a changed answer replaces are answered as superseded
